children: GCM Grosvenor and Hyperion Realty Capital are teaming up, with plans to own a portfolio of shopping centers anchored by grocery stores across the western U.S.

GCM Grosvenor, an asset manager specializing in middle market real estate, will kick off the partnership with an investment of up to $100 million into a new closed-end vehicle targeting $200 million of equity, the companies said Friday.
As part of the partnership, GCM Grosvenor will join Hyperion's board.

The companies said they would focus on middle-market assets that have historically attracted less institutional capital than larger-format retail investments, with plans to invest in neighborhood, strip and community centers representing up to about $1 billion in aggregate property value as additional investment partners join the fund.
Hyperion currently owns and operates 10 shopping centers across the west coast.
